race_context: The district: Southwestern Consolidated School District of Shelby County is a small K-12 district with its office at 3406 W. 600 S., Shelbyville {sw_home}. It runs Southwestern Elementary, Southwestern Jr./Sr. High School and the Little Spartans Preschool {sw_home}. The junior-senior high school is about 7 miles southwest of Shelbyville and had 280 students in 2023–24, according to federal data cited by Wikipedia {wiki_swhs}. Superintendent Dr. Jamison Wilkins reported a fall 2025 count-day enrollment of 599 students, not counting preschool {sw_min_oct25}. In September 2026 he said the district expected record enrollment (at least since 2020), with about 20 more K-12 students than the year before {at_sep26}. On March 11, 2026 the board voted 7-0 for a new contract for Wilkins, with a condition that he gets no raise in a year when teachers get none {sw_min_mar26}.

The board: there are seven members {sw_board}{sw_min_jan26}. They are President Jon Deater, Vice President Blake Newkirk, Secretary Dustin Simpson, John Blue, Daryl Thomas, Derrek Tennell and Brad Stamper {sw_board}{sw_min_jan26}. Seats are tied to townships, plus one at-large seat {at_2024_results}{sn_2024_goals}. In 2024, Daryl Thomas defeated incumbent Travis Beck for a Hendricks Township seat, 950 votes to 915 {at_2024_results}{sn_2024_goals}. Jonathan Deater and John Blue won the two Jackson Township seats in an uncontested race {sn_2024_goals}{at_2024_results}. The 2026 ballot has three races: At Large, Hendricks Township and Washington Township {in_list}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: current members Brad Stamper (running at large) and Derrek Tennell (running in Washington Township) are on the ballot {sw_board}{in_list}. Tennell first joined the board by appointment in March 2022 {sn_2022_supt}. Two members said they will not run again {sw_min_aug25}{sw_min_jun26}. Blake Newkirk said so at the Aug. 13, 2025 meeting {sw_min_aug25}, and Dustin Simpson said so at the June 10, 2026 meeting {sw_min_jun26}. Doug Swift is the only candidate for the Hendricks Township seat {in_list}. This guide did not find 2022 results or a district source showing which seat each current member holds.

Seat count is uncertain {in_list}{sn_2024_goals}. Three of the seven members were elected in 2024, which suggests four seats end this year {in_list}{sn_2024_goals}. The state list, however, shows three races, each 'vote for 1' {in_list}{sn_2024_goals}. If Washington Township has two seats on the ballot, both of its candidates would be elected. This guide did not find a 2026 sample ballot or county candidate list to confirm the number of seats in each race.

Budget, staffing and property taxes (2025–2026): at an Oct. 29, 2025 hearing on the tentative teacher contract, Wilkins said the deal lowered the starting teacher salary to $46,000 and that staff cuts might come the next year to help cover salary and benefit costs {sw_min_oct29}. Newkirk asked residents unhappy about the reduced funding to contact their state legislators {sw_min_oct29}. The teachers association president told the board on Nov. 12, 2025 that 'with the changes made by the state, this would be a fiscally challenging year' {sw_min_nov25}. On May 13, 2026 the board voted 7-0 to cut four positions: a high school health/PE job, the elementary assistant principal, an elementary teaching job and an instructional assistant {sw_min_may26}. In June it ended one contract through a reduction in force {sw_min_jun26}.

Assessed value and the 2027 budget: in September 2026 Wilkins said the district's assessed value was about $389 million, down roughly $18 million to $19 million from the year before {at_sep26}. He attributed much of the drop to SEA 1 and changes affecting farmland {at_sep26}. No one commented at the budget hearing, and the board was expected to adopt the 2027 budget in October {at_sep26}. The 2026 budget was adopted 7-0 on Oct. 15, 2025 {sw_min_oct25}.

Facilities (2025–2026): the board paid for a roofing project in 2025 {sw_min_aug25}{sw_min_oct25}. On Nov. 12, 2025 it approved bids for an HVAC project paid for with GO bonds: $180,000 for general trades, $3,189,000 for HVAC and $314,900 for electrical {sw_min_nov25}. The construction manager said the work would be done by the start of the August 2026 school year {sw_min_nov25}. Bond project payments went on through summer 2026, including $1,307,328.65 to the HVAC contractor {sw_min_jul26}{sw_min_aug26}.

Academics (2025–2026): in September 2025 the district set goals of 48% ILEARN proficiency in English and 45% in math {sw_min_sep25}. Wilkins said current results were 46.3% and 42.7% {sw_min_sep25}. On the redesigned 2026 ILEARN, 33.5% of Southwestern students in grades 3–8 were proficient in both English and math {at_oct26}. That was above the statewide rate of 31.5% and second among Shelby County districts {at_oct26}. Wilkins said Southwestern Elementary was one of three schools in the state with a 100% IREAD passing rate {sw_min_apr26}. The high school received a $50,000 Project Lead The Way Biomedical Sciences startup grant {sw_min_mar26}.

Enrollment and school choice (2025–2026): the board approved moving 6th grade to the junior-senior high school starting in 2026–27 {sw_min_aug25}. It approved an out-of-district enrollment policy for 2026–27 in March 2026 {sw_min_mar26}. In May 2026 it created the Spartan Virtual Academy for grades 6–12, run through Edmentum {sw_min_may26}{at_may26}. Eleven students had enrolled in the online academy by July 2026 {sw_min_jul26}.

Policies and planning: the board held community brainstorming nights in April 2025 {sw_min_mar25ws} and approved a strategic plan 7-0 on Aug. 13, 2025 {sw_min_aug25}. In May 2026 it approved a stricter high school cellphone rule tied to new state law: phones must be put away all day, including on buses {at_may26}. On May 13, 2026 the board voted 7-0 to continue a partnership with Girls Inc. for its Healthy Sexuality Program and to approve the 'I Decide For Me' curriculum for the high school human sexuality unit {sw_min_may26}.

County tournaments (June 2026): at the June 10, 2026 meeting, members of the public and board members objected to the cancellation of the Shelby County tournaments after Shelby Eastern schools withdrew {sw_min_jun26}. Wilkins said the athletic directors from Morristown and Waldron had chosen to withdraw and that no formal rules prevented it {sw_min_jun26}.

Party labels: under a recent state law change, school board candidates now declare a party or a 'non-disclosed' status {at_dec25}. A Triton Central board president told a December 2025 county meeting that a declared party can decide who fills a seat that becomes vacant mid-term {at_dec25}. On the state list, Tennell is labeled Republican and the other three candidates Nonpartisan {in_list}.
Forums: this guide found no candidate forums, questionnaires or news profiles of the 2026 Southwestern candidates.

background: Current member of the Southwestern school board {sw_board}. He was the board's representative to Blue River Career Programs until August 2025, when Tennell replaced him because of scheduling conflicts {sw_min_aug25}.
path_to_ballot: Listed as Nonpartisan on the state candidate list {in_list}.

items: Moved to adopt the 2026 budget, which passed 7-0 on Oct. 15, 2025 {sw_min_oct25}.
Moved to approve the HVAC project bids, which passed 6-0 on Nov. 12, 2025 {sw_min_nov25}.
Seconded approval of the 2025–26 master teacher contract, which passed 6-0 on Nov. 12, 2025 {sw_min_nov25}.

candidates.summary: Incumbent board member (Derrek Tennell) running in Washington Township, listed as Republican {sw_board}{in_list}. He was board president in 2025 {sw_min_aug25}{sw_min_jan26}.
background: Joined the Southwestern board by appointment {sn_2022_supt}. His first meeting was in March 2022, when he abstained on the superintendent hire because, he said, he had not been part of the decision process {sn_2022_supt}.
Was board president in 2025 {sw_min_aug25}{sw_min_oct25}. He became the board's representative to Blue River Career Programs in August 2025 {sw_min_aug25}.
Recognized at the April 15, 2026 meeting for receiving the Advanced Individual Award from the Indiana Association of School Boards {sw_min_apr26}.
path_to_ballot: Listed as Republican on the state candidate list {in_list}.

items: Moved to approve the four position cuts, which passed 7-0 on May 13, 2026 {sw_min_may26}. Moved to approve the superintendent's contract with the condition that he gets no raise in a year when teachers get none (passed 7-0, March 11, 2026) {sw_min_mar26}.

Moved to approve the Spartan Virtual School guidelines for grades 6–12 (passed 7-0, May 13, 2026) {sw_min_may26}. On Aug. 12, 2026 he said out-of-district transfers were 'a positive look for the future' {sw_min_aug26}.
Moved to continue the Girls Inc {sw_min_may26}. Healthy Sexuality Program partnership for 2026–27 (passed 7-0, May 13, 2026) {sw_min_may26}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member {sw_min_aug25}. In August 2025 he said the district's path 'has improved immensely over the past four years' {sw_min_aug25}. In June 2026 he said the decision to end the county tournaments was made by a small number of people {sw_min_jun26}.
